We can just make all of host dispatcher methods demand required options. That avoid future mistakes where we don't forward options properly from public API to dispatcher.

E.g. 
```diff
-options?: ?PreloadModuleImplOptions,
+options?: Required<PreloadModuleImplOptions>,
```

that should apply to `preload`, `preloadModule`, `preinitStyle`, `preinitScript`, and `preinitModuleScript`.

Can you take care of that? The PR also needs a rebase.

What happens when I add an event listener as passive and remove it as non-passive? The spec makes it sound like each add would overwrite if only `passive` changes and removing should ignore `passive`.

Great question — you're right per the DOM spec.

The [DOM Living Standard §2.9.4](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener) says that the listener identity tuple is `(type, callback, capture)` — **`passive` and `once` are NOT part of the identity key**. So:

- `addEventListener('click', fn, {passive: false})` and `addEventListener('click', fn, {passive: true})` are the **same listener** (same capture=false) — the second call is a no-op
- `removeEventListener('click', fn)` removes it regardless of what `passive` was set to

I've updated the fix in commit `fcefce9` to key only on `capture` (dropping `once` and `passive` from the key string), and added a new test (`47cd78d`) that verifies:
1. Two adds with `passive: false` and `passive: true` are treated as the same listener (second is a no-op)
2. `removeEventListener` without any passive option removes the listener

This now matches the spec behavior exactly. Thanks for catching that!

The test should make it clear which handler is fired: The first or second one? By spec, the second handler shouldn't have been appended:
> The [event listener](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener) is appended to target’s [event listener list](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-event-listener-list) and is not appended if it has the same [type](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#event-listener-type), [callback](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#event-listener-callback), and [capture](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#event-listener-capture).

-- https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener:~:text=The%20event%20listener%20is%20appended%20to%20target%E2%80%99s%20event%20listener%20list%20and%20is%20not%20appended%20if%20it%20has%20the%20same%20type%2C%20callback%2C%20and%20capture.

It also looks like there's some asymmetry with removing. For adding we just look at `capture`. But removing apparently looks at all the options:

> Removes the [event listener](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener) in target’s [event listener list](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-event-listener-list) with the same type, callback, and options.

-- https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-listener:~:text=Removes%20the%20event%20listener%20in%20target%E2%80%99s%20event%20listener%20list%20with%20the%20same%20type%2C%20callback%2C%20and%20options.

Can you do some testing how popular browsers behave?

There are browsers that support `performance.measure` but not passing a `measureOptions` object to it, for example, Chromium engine on LG TVs prior to 2021 and on Samsung TVs prior to 2022

In such cases, React fails with `Error: Failed to execute 'measure' on 'Performance': The mark '[object Object]' does not exist`
You would need to polyfill `performance.measure` for this case. The `measureOptions` parameter has been supported in all modern browsers, since 2022.
